correctness.rationale: For every 0<R<=pi, alpha>0, Peter-Weyl reduces positivity to b_l=(J_l-J_{l+1})/pi with J_n=integral_0^R (R-theta)^alpha cos(n theta)dtheta; this follows exactly from (1-cos theta)chi_l=cos(l theta)-cos((l+1)theta) and Haar density. At alpha=2, J_n=2R/n^2-2sin(nR)/n^3 (n>=1); h(x)=(x-sin x)/x^3 is strictly decreasing by sign of 2x+x cos x-3 sin x, while b_0>0 by direct integral. For alpha>2 a positive beta-mixture of alpha=2 kernels preserves strict spectral positivity. Completeness of irreducible matrix coefficients then gives strict finite-set positive definiteness. For 0<alpha<2, endpoint asymptotics imply b_l=(2 Gamma(alpha+1)sin(R/2)/(pi l^(alpha+1)))sin((l+1/2)R-pi(alpha+1)/2)+o(l^(-alpha-1)); the origin contribution to consecutive differences is O(l^-3) and cannot mask nonzero oscillatory negative subsequences. Irrational R/(2pi) yields density 1/2 negative; rational radii admit recurring negative phases, including R=pi. Independent 1556 finite Fourier/coefficient diagnostics at four radii and alpha=0.6,1,1.4 support but do not prove these infinite statements.
residual_risks: Infinite phase-density and endpoint asymptotics rest on the analytic derivation, not the finite diagnostics.
No claim is made for alpha<=0, R>pi, or different metrics on other groups.
